title: Silently crash on GetQuotaObjectForFile
body: I am using 64-bit Firefox 115 on Windows 7 SP1. While uploading 16 videos totaling about 64 GB to YouTube in Private Browsing, the whole browser silently crashes after a while. There is no crash reporter window and about:crashes has no recent entry. Retrying produced three crashes before I completed the upload. This did not happen the same way in Firefox 114. I disabled HTTP/3 to get full upload speed. Every crash has access violation 0xc0000005 in xul.dll at GetQuotaObjectForFile in QuotaVFS.cpp; WinDbg shows the fault while dereferencing a pointer at line 616. I want the crash fixed; the expected result is that Firefox does not crash.

symptoms_visible: While I upload many large videos to YouTube in Private Browsing, Firefox 115 silently exits after a while.
No crash reporter window appears, and about:crashes contains no recent crash.
WinDbg catches 0xc0000005 in xul.dll at GetQuotaObjectForFile while an address is being dereferenced.
N0.label: N0 silent Private Browsing crash reported

symptoms_visible: With a clean profile, two normal-browsing batches of 15 two-gigabyte videos finish without a crash.
With the same files in Private Browsing, Firefox 115.0.3 ESR crashes while starting the sixth file.
N1.label: N1 crash isolated to Private Browsing

symptoms_visible: The crash occurs with free space still available on the system drive.
Large uploads in Private Browsing worked in Firefox versions before 115, apart from older tab crashes when RAM overflowed.
N2.label: N2 disk capacity and prior behavior established

symptoms_visible: In the private IndexedDB storage directory, five files grow to about 9.9 GB in total.
When the sixth upload starts, a sixth file appears and quickly disappears; several seconds later Firefox crashes.
Immediately before another crash I had about 10.4 GB free, and immediately afterward about 14.4 GB was free.
N3.label: N3 quota-boundary behavior and wrong cast identified

symptoms_visible: I have not reported a retest on my own system with a build containing the landed fix, so I cannot yet confirm that the large Private Browsing upload no longer crashes.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal fix landed without reporter retest

question_patterns: Does the crash reproduce only in Private Browsing, or does the same upload also crash in a normal window?
Can you compare the same upload in normal and Private Browsing using a clean profile?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested with a clean profile where the significant change was disabling HTTP/3. In normal browsing I uploaded two batches of 15 videos, 2 GB each, without a crash. In Private Browsing, Firefox crashed while trying to upload the sixth file in the first batch.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same clean-profile upload crashes at the same point in both normal and Private Browsing.
Private Browsing crashes on the seventh file instead of the sixth, while all 15 finish in normal browsing.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c9-c12: participant2 asked whether Private Browsing was involved; the reporter then performed clean-profile comparisons on Firefox 115.0.3 ESR. The precise crash point was added by the reporter and is represented as target-node volunteered information.

question_patterns: How much free space is left on the system drive when this happens?
Can you check the available disk space around the time of the Private Browsing crash?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I had 20.3 GB free on the system drive. The crash happened after less than 11 GB had been uploaded in Private Browsing. On another run there was 10.4 GB free shortly before the crash, and 14.4 GB free immediately afterward.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The system drive reaches zero free bytes before every crash.
There is about 18 GB free rather than 20.3 GB, and several gigabytes are freed after the crash.

question_patterns: Did the same large upload work in Private Browsing before Firefox 115, or only in normal browsing?
Which browsing mode worked in Firefox versions earlier than 115?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The upload worked in Private Browsing before Firefox 115. Older versions could have tab crashes when RAM overflowed, but Firefox 115 can suddenly crash the whole browser.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Private Browsing has always crashed this way, including in Firefox 114 and earlier.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c13-c16: participant3 asked for free disk space and whether pre-115 success was in Private or normal browsing. The reporter supplied the measurements and noted that the crash occurs before the disk is full.

solution.intent: Diagnose the access violation as an invalid VFS cast: the direct QuotaVFS assumption is unsafe when Private Browsing IndexedDB uses ObfuscatingVFS and forwards operations to QuotaVFS.
solution.concrete_example: The static cast in GetQuotaObjectForFile works when IndexedDB uses QuotaVFS directly, but Private Browsing goes through ObfuscatingVFS, so treating the forwarded sqlite file as the direct QuotaVFS type can dereference the wrong object.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the faulting instruction and established that the crash is specific to Private Browsing. Identifying that Private Browsing's ObfuscatingVFS forwards to QuotaVFS and makes the static cast invalid was participant4's engineering diagnosis in c15, not a conclusion produced by the reporter.

edges.comment: Reporter system plus participant4 diagnosis, c15-c22: participant4 identified the static cast as invalid for the ObfuscatingVFS forwarding path. The reporter subsequently monitored the private IndexedDB files and volunteered the approximately 10 GB boundary and disappearing sixth-file observations. The reporter's alternative freed-object speculation is not treated as the accepted root cause.

solution.intent: Fix the Private Browsing IndexedDB crash by removing the invalid VFS cast and obtaining quota objects through the correct QuotaVFS/ObfuscatingVFS interface, then ask the reporter to verify a build containing the landed change.
solution.concrete_example: Use the proper VFS-specific function instead of statically treating the forwarded ObfuscatingVFS file as a direct QuotaVFS file. The change was landed in mozilla-central; please retest the same large Private Browsing upload in a current build and report whether Firefox remains running when storage approaches the quota boundary.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers linked the roughly 10 GB group-quota behavior to the cleanup or quota-error path that reaches GetQuotaObjectForFile. The final accepted defect is the invalid cast between the ObfuscatingVFS and QuotaVFS representations, not the reporter's tentative theory that cleanup freed a live object.

edges.comment: Participant3 and landing automation, c25-c29: patches described as fixing the wrong cast and declaring the relevant VFS functions landed. The reporter did not subsequently test a fixed build, so this terminal thread state records landing without claiming user-verified resolution. Performance-alert discussion in c30 is omitted as unrelated logistics.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: Private Browsing IndexedDB uses ObfuscatingVFS, which forwards to QuotaVFS, and GetQuotaObjectForFile performed an invalid cast that could dereference the wrong object.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: the repeatable Private-versus-normal comparison, the GetQuotaObjectForFile access violation, available disk space, and the approximately 10 GB private IndexedDB boundary behavior.

Must not treat ordinary disk exhaustion, the crash reporter failure, or the reporter's tentative freed-object theory as the root cause; freeing disk space alone is not the code fix established by the thread.
The corrective action must replace the unsafe cast with VFS-safe quota-object access for the ObfuscatingVFS-to-QuotaVFS path.
Must ask the reporter to retest the same workload on a build containing the fix and must not declare the issue user-verified, because the thread contains no affected-user confirmation after landing.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly persistent and technically capable reporter who can reproduce long-running storage failures, inspect profile files, monitor disk and memory use, attach WinDbg to the correct Firefox process, and interpret native stack and register output, but offers tentative causal theories rather than claiming source-level certainty.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct, terse, and evidence-heavy; provides repeated controlled tests and raw debugger output, prioritizes browser stability over crash-reporting logistics, and clearly labels uncertain explanations as guesses.
